17625-artificial-light-its-influence-upo.title: Its Influence Upon Civilization
17625-artificial-light-its-influence-upo.creator: M. Luckiesh
17625-artificial-light-its-influence-upo.description: A book by M. Luckiesh. The human race was born in slavery, totally subservient to nature. The earliest primitive beings feasted or starved according to nature's bounty and sweltered or shivered according to the weather. When night fell they sought shelter with animal instinct, for not only were activities almost completely curtailed by darkness but beyond its screen lurked many dangers.

5577-a-word-only-a-word-complete.title: A Word Only A Word Complete
5577-a-word-only-a-word-complete.creator: Georg Ebers
5577-a-word-only-a-word-complete.description: A book by Georg Ebers. replied Ruth, arranging the dry sticks. “He toils hard, but not for gold and gain, to find the right words. You are always wanting to know what he is looking for in his big books, so I plucked up courage to ask him, and now I know.

arxiv-2105-03233.title: Regression on Deep Visual Features using Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) to Predict Hydraulic Blockage at Culverts
arxiv-2105-03233.creator: Umair Iqbal, Johan Barthelemy, Pascal Perez, Wanqing Li
arxiv-2105-03233.description: Abstract Cross drainage hydraulic structures (i.e., culverts, bridges) in urban landscapes are prone to getting blocked by transported debris which often results in causing the flash floods. In context of Australia, Wollongong City Council (WCC) blockage conduit policy is the only formal guideline to consider blockage in design process.

arxiv-2211-02542.title: Self-Supervised Learning for Speech Enhancement Through Synthesis
arxiv-2211-02542.creator: Bryce Irvin, Marko Stamenovic, Mikolaj Kegler, Li-Chia Yang
arxiv-2211-02542.description: Abstract Modern speech enhancement (SE) networks typically implement noise suppression through time-frequency masking, latent representation masking, or discriminative signal prediction. In contrast, some recent works explore SE via generative speech synthesis, where the system’s output is synthesized by a neural vocoder after an inherently lossy feature-denoising step.

arxiv-2302-03768.title: Catch Me If You Can: Improving Adversaries in Cyber-Security With Q-Learning Algorithms
arxiv-2302-03768.creator: Arti Bandhana 1 , Ondřej Lukáš 1 , Sebastian Garcia 2 and Tomáš Kroupa 2 Czech Technical University bandhart@fel.cvut.cz, lukasond@fel.cvut.cz, sebastian.garcia@agents.fel.cvut.cz, tomas.kroupa@fel.cvut.cz
arxiv-2302-03768.description: Abstract The ongoing rise in cyberattacks and the lack of skilled professionals in the cybersecurity domain to combat these attacks show the need for automated tools capable of detecting an attack with good performance. Attackers disguise their actions and launch attacks that consist of multiple actions, which are difficult to detect.

arxiv-2303-04544.title: Models of symbol emergence in communication: a conceptual review and a guide for avoiding local minima
arxiv-2303-04544.creator: Julian Zubek, Tomasz Korbak, Joanna Rączaszek-Leonardi
arxiv-2303-04544.description: Abstract Computational simulations are a popular method for testing hypotheses about the emergence of communication. This kind of research is performed in a variety of traditions including language evolution, developmental psychology, cognitive science, machine learning, robotics, etc. The motivations for the models are different, but the operationalizations and methods used are often similar.

arxiv-2409-12223.title: Lie algebraic invariants in quantum linear optics
arxiv-2409-12223.creator: Pablo V. Parellada, Vicent Gimeno i Garcia, Julio José Moyano-Fernández, Juan Carlos Garcia-Escartin
arxiv-2409-12223.description: Abstract Quantum linear optics is a promising candidate for obtaining a quantum computational advantage. However, linear optics without post-selection is not powerful enough to produce any quantum state from a given input state. This limits its utility since some computations require entangled resources that are difficult to prepare. Thus, we need a deeper understanding of linear optical state preparation.

arxiv-2411-17713.title: Llama Guard 3-1B-INT4: Compact and Efficient Safeguard for Human-AI Conversations
arxiv-2411-17713.creator: Igor Fedorov, Kate Plawiak, Lemeng Wu, Tarek Elgamal, Naveen Suda, Eric Smith, Hongyuan Zhan, Jianfeng Chi, Yuriy Hulovatyy, Kimish Patel, Zechun Liu, Changsheng Zhao, Yangyang Shi, Tijmen Blankenvoort, Mahesh Pasupuleti, Bilge Soran, Zacharie Delpierre Coudert, Rachad Alao, Raghuraman Krishnamoorth
arxiv-2411-17713.description: Abstract This paper presents Llama Guard 3-1B-INT4, a compact and efficient Llama Guard model, which has been open-sourced to the community during Meta Connect 2024. We demonstrate that Llama Guard 3-1B-INT4 can be deployed on resource-constrained devices, achieving a throughput of at least 30 tokens per second and a time-to-first-token of 2.

arxiv-2502-01742.title: Constraining the geometry of the gas surrounding a typical galaxy at z = 3.4 z=3.4 with Ly α \alpha polarization
arxiv-2502-01742.creator: A. Bolamperti, S.-J. Chang, J. Vernet, A. Zanella, M. Gronke, F. Arrigoni Battaia, F. Calura, E. Iani, E. Vanzella
arxiv-2502-01742.description: Abstract Lyman- α \alpha (Ly α \alpha ) emission is the intrinsically strongest tracer of recombining ionized hydrogen in young, star-forming galaxies, but its origin is still debated. Ly α \alpha arises when emitted photons scatter in neutral hydrogen, with each scattering event changing their propagation direction and frequency.

arxiv-2502-07050.title: Artificial General Intelligence and the End of Human Employment: The Need to Renegotiate the Social Contract
arxiv-2502-07050.creator: Pascal Stiefenhofer
arxiv-2502-07050.description: Abstract The emergence of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) labor, including AI agents and autonomous systems operating at near-zero marginal cost, reduces the marginal productivity of human labor, ultimately pushing wages toward zero. As AGI labor and capital replace human workers, economic power shifts to capital owners, resulting in extreme wealth concentration, rising inequality, and reduced social mobility.

arxiv-2506-05913.title: Optimal designs for identifying effective doses in drug combination studies
arxiv-2506-05913.creator: Leonie Schürmeyer, Ludger Sandig, Leonie Theresa Hezler, Bernd-Wolfgang Igl, Kirsten Schorning
arxiv-2506-05913.description: Abstract We consider the optimal design problem for identifying effective dose combinations within drug combination studies where the effect of the combination of two drugs is investigated. Drug combination studies are becoming increasingly important as they investigate potential interaction effects rather than the individual impacts of the drugs.

arxiv-2506-16261.title: Global well-posedness for 2D compressible radially symmetric Navier-Stokes equations with swirl
arxiv-2506-16261.creator: Xiangdi Huang, Weili Meng* a. State Key Laboratory of Mathematical Sciences, Academy of MathematicsSystems Science,Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing 100190, China;
arxiv-2506-16261.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the radially symmetric compressible Navier-Stokes equations with swirl in two-dimensional disks, where the shear viscosity coefficient μ = const > 0 \mu=\text{const}>0 , and the bulk one λ = ρ β ​ ( β > 0 ) \lambda=\rho^{\beta}(\beta>0) .

arxiv-2507-05813.title: Adaptive Communication Through Exploiting RIS, SSK, and CIM for Improved Reliability and Efficiency
arxiv-2507-05813.creator: Ferhat Bayar, Onur Salan, Erdogan Aydin, Haci Ilhan
arxiv-2507-05813.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a novel communication system model that integrates reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), spatial shift keying (SSK), and code index modulation (CIM) based on Hadamard coding called RIS based transmit SSK-CIM (RIS-CIM-TSSK). By leveraging RIS, the system adapts rapidly to dynamic environments, enhancing error rates and overall reliability.

arxiv-2508-12098.creator: Ahmet Umut Çoraplı, Burcu Bektaş Demirci, Nurettin Cenk Turgay
arxiv-2508-12098.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ahmet Umut Çoraplı, Burcu Bektaş Demirci, Nurettin Cenk Turgay. arxiv-2511-17240.title: A Fast Binary Splitting Approach for Non-Adaptive Learning of Erdős–Rényi Graphs
arxiv-2511-17240.creator: Hoang Ta and Jonathan Scarlett
arxiv-2511-17240.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hoang Ta and Jonathan Scarlett. We study the problem of learning an unknown graph via group queries on node subsets, where each query reports whether at least one edge is present among the queried nodes.

pmc-11560856.title: Bridging the species divide: The limits of rat models in capturing human PVOD mechanisms
pmc-11560856.creator: Frédéric Perros, Cédric Chaveroux, David Montani
pmc-11560856.description: SR and protein kinase R (PKR) in an experimental rat model, provide compelling evidence for potential therapeutic strategies to mitigate pulmonary vascular remodeling in PVOD, in both young and aged rats. The study is a significant step forward in understanding disease mechanisms, and the authors have executed an impressive investigation into the ISR's role.

pmc-11616867.title: Effectiveness of manual dexterity assessment methods for preclinical training in Dentistry
pmc-11616867.creator: Luis Eduardo Genaro, Tamíris da Costa Neves, Júlia Margato Pazos, Lívia Nordi Dovigo, Patrícia P. N. S. Garcia
pmc-11616867.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveThis study aimed to verify the predictive capacity of manual dexterity assessment methods for pre-clinical training in Dentistry.MethodStudents from the fifth year of the undergraduate course in Dentistry (N = 95) participated in this study. Manual dexterity was investigated as a variable of interest, measured by the O’Connor Finger Dexterity Test methods—Model 32021, Purdue Pegboard Test—Model 32020A, Dental Manual Dexterity Assessment—DMDA, Class One Cavity Preparation Assessent—COCA and Class One Composite Resin Restoration Assessment—COCRA.

pmc-11624606.title: Machine Learning Models for Predicting 24-Hour Intraocular Pressure Changes: A Comparative Study
pmc-11624606.creator: Chen Ranran, Lei Jinming, Liao Yujie, Jin Yiping, Wang Xue, Li Hong, Bi Yanlong, Zhu Haohao
pmc-11624606.description: BackgroundPredicting 24-hour intraocular pressure (IOP) fluctuations is crucial for enhancing glaucoma management. Traditional methods of measuring 24-hour IOP fluctuations are complex and present certain limitations. The present study leverages machine learning techniques to forecast 24-hour IOP fluctuations based on daytime IOP measurements.Material/MethodsA binary method was used to classify 24-hour IOP fluctuations as either >8 mmHg or ≤8 mmHg.

pmc-12822120.title: Evaluation of anemia and iron status in Japanese patients with gynecological malignancy: retrospective cohort study
pmc-12822120.creator: Tetsuya Kokabu, Saiko Yamauchi, Miho Iwai, Kota Aoki, Ayaka Okamura, Yosuke Tarumi, Hisashi Kataoka, Kaori Yoriki, Taisuke Mori
pmc-12822120.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAnemia and iron deficiency are common among patients with cancer and can have a significant impact on their prognosis. However, the current status of anemia and iron deficiency in Japanese patients with gynecological malignancies remains unclear. This study aimed to clarify the prevalence of anemia and iron deficiency at the time of diagnosis and to evaluate their influence on hemoglobin levels during cancer treatment in Japanese patients with gynecological malignancies.MethodsEligible patients were those diagnosed with gynecological cancers.

pmc-13079510.title: Performance of an artificial intelligence–based software in detecting pneumothorax on supine chest radiographs: a retrospective study
pmc-13079510.creator: Hitomi Nakamura, Tomoki Wada, Ryota Inokuchi, Shouhei Hanaoka, Naoya Sakamoto, Kent Doi
pmc-13079510.description: PurposeTo evaluate the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-based software for pneumothorax detection on supine radiographs and its impact on physicians’ interpretation.MethodsThis single-center retrospective study analyzed 114 hemithoraces with pneumothorax and 340 without, using computed tomography as the reference standard.

pmc-13092070.title: The self-assembly mechanisms of glycyrrhizic acid: Permeation enhancement and transdermal applications
pmc-13092070.creator: Lin Zhou, Youran Deng, Mingjie Ou, Zhuxian Wang
pmc-13092070.description: Glycyrrhizic acid (GA) is an amphiphilic triterpenoid saponin compound derived from licorice. This review first summarizes the behaviors and evolution mechanisms of GA forming different nanostructures (dimers, micelles, nanoparticles, nanofibers, and hydrogels) under varying conditions (concentration, temperature, pH, ionic strength) and intermolecular forces. Subsequently, it introduces the transdermal permeation enhancement and bioavailability improvement of hydrophobic drugs when encapsulated by GA.

pmc-13190318.title: Catabolism of extracellular glutathione supplies cysteine to support tumours
pmc-13190318.creator: Fabio Hecht, Marco Zocchi, Emily T. Tuttle, Nathan P. Ward, Fatemeh Alimohammadi, Amal Afzal Khan, Veronica C. Gomes, Bradley Smith, Jennifer J. Twardowski, Bradley N. Mills, Kevin A. Welle, Sina Ghaemmaghami, Zhuoran Zhou, Yuhan Gan, Yun Pyo Kang, Juliana Cazarin, Zamira G. Soares, Mete Emir Ozgurs
pmc-13190318.description: Restricting amino acids from tumours is an emerging therapeutic strategy with substantial promise1. Although typically considered an intracellular antioxidant with tumour-promoting capabilities2, glutathione (GSH), as a tripeptide of cysteine, glutamate and glycine, can be catabolized to release amino acids. The extent to which GSH-derived amino acids are essential to cancers is unclear.

pmc-13416184.title: Determining behavioral proxies of preference: mate choice and the New England Cottontail (Sylvilagus transitionalis)
pmc-13416184.creator: Hannah Petit, Vivian Stansell, Louis Perrotti, Justin T Richard, Karen Mabry
pmc-13416184.description: Reintroduction breeding programs are a key conservation strategy that can be more successful when breeding pairs are determined through mate choice. The vulnerable New England Cottontail (NEC) (Sylvilagus transitionalis) has lost much of its historic range, prompting the establishment of a program to release zoo-bred rabbits to bolster declining populations.

pmc-13551047.title: Bionic vision technologies: progress and perspectives on retinal prostheses and optogenetics for the treatment of advanced retinal degeneration
pmc-13551047.creator: Na Long, Meng Si, Yin Jiang, Fan Chen, Bei Chen, Fei Jiang, Shangang Pan, Xueqin Chu, Huarong Wu
pmc-13551047.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Advanced degenerative retinal diseases [e.g., retinitis pigmentosa (RP) and age-related macular degeneration (AMD)] are characterized by irreversible photoreceptor loss, and conventional interventions rarely prevent progression to profound vision loss at advanced stages. Retinal prostheses and optogenetic therapies are two leading bionic strategies to bypass absent photoreceptors, yet both are limited by a shared “encoding–biointerface” bottleneck: converting external scenes into interpretable neural activity in surviving retinal circuits with adequate selectivity, safety margins, and long-term stability.

pmc-13615042.title: Endovascular Treatment for Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Methodological Systematic Review of Health Economic Decision Modeling Studies
pmc-13615042.creator: Andreas Beisel, Hans-Helmut König, Judith Dams
pmc-13615042.description: Background and ObjectiveIschemic strokes are one of the main causes for death and disability worldwide and pose a substantial economic burden on healthcare systems. Currently, endovascular treatment is considered one of the most effective therapeutic options for the acute treatment of ischemic strokes.

the-dream-detective.title: The Dream Detective

the-dream-detective.description: Ten stories featuring perhaps the most fantastic sleuth of them all: Moris Klaw, the Dream Detective.
